candidates.claim: The PR now follows `*_links` `next` for the ports and routers lists, but the sibling Neutron list calls that feed the router list (router interface ports by device_id) and the lookups by id (networks, subnets, security-groups) still read only the first page. With a `pagination_max_limit` lower than the 50-id chunk (or a router with several interfaces: 50 routers x N interface ports), results are silently truncated: private networks / names go missing in the router list, and the lookups return a partial list that is treated as complete (best-effort fallback to IDs). The new docs/comments claim the returned list is complete on paginated deployments.
candidates.evidence: Code at 86a355a8: fetchRouterInterfacePorts does `const response = await network.get(withQuery(PORTS_BASE_URL, params))` then `parseOrThrow(RouterInterfacePortSummaryListResponseSchema, data, ...).ports` with no `next` handling; listInterfaces (routersRouter.ts:359-366) does `network.get(withQuery(PORTS_BASE_URL, portParams))` and `const { ports } = parseOrThrow(RouterPortListResponseSchema, ...)` likewise; lookupHelpers.ts fetchNetworkSummaries/fetchSubnetSummaries/fetchSecurityGroupSummaries each issue one GET per chunk of 50 ids and read only `.networks`/`.subnets`/`.security_groups`. Reference (https://docs.openstack.org/api-ref/network/v2/#pagination, read from neutron-lib api-ref/source/v2/intro.inc): "To reduce load on the service, list operations will return a maximum number of items at a time." and "If the client requests a limit beyond the maximum limit configured by the deployment, the server returns the maximum limit number of items." and "For convenience, list responses contain atom ``next`` links and ``previous`` links. The last page in the list requested with ``page_reverse=False`` will not contain ``next`` link". The id filter on list calls does not lift the cap. Only the ports/routers top-level lists got the loop in this PR (delta: requestHelpers.nextPageUrl, portsRouter.ts, routersRouter.ts). Note: these lines are not in delta.diff (listInterfaces blame ca33c0169); they matter because the PR adds the claim 'the returned list is complete' (docs/0010_routers_bff.md) and the ports list reuses the same lookups.
candidates.precedent: The PR's own loop in routersRouter.list / portsRouter.list shows the intended pattern.

candidates.claim: Pagination follows `next` by reusing only the query string of the absolute href against the BFF base path, and the list schemas accept `ports_links`/`routers_links` as optional arrays. Reference documents the links field as `*_links` with rel next/previous; consistent. However the guard `visited` silently stops and returns a partial list (no error) if Neutron returns a repeating next URL, so the user sees a truncated list without any signal.
candidates.evidence: Code: `while (nextUrl && !visited.has(nextUrl)) { visited.add(nextUrl) ...`; same loop in routersRouter.ts. Reference https://docs.openstack.org/api-ref/network/v2/#pagination: 'The last page in the list requested with page_reverse=False will not contain next link' - the documented termination is the absence of `next`; the code adds a silent cut-off on a repeated URL instead of failing. Also no `limit` is sent, so the page size is the deployment default/maximum (doc: 'the server returns the maximum limit number of items'); a project with many ports means many sequential requests (no upper bound on pages) before any response is returned.

candidates.claim: The new Neutron pagination loop in ports.list (and routers.list) has no upper bound on pages or accumulated items. The `visited` set only stops a repeated identical URL, so a `next` link whose marker keeps changing (or a very large project) makes one tRPC query issue unbounded sequential Neutron requests and buffer every result in BFF memory before the network/subnet lookups. Any authenticated user can trigger it by opening the list page.
candidates.evidence: git show 86a355a8:packages/aurora/src/server/Network/routers/portsRouter.ts: loop pushes `...pagePorts` into `ports` until `nextPageUrl` returns undefined or a URL repeats; no max-page or max-item cap. Same pattern in routersRouter.ts list. nextPageUrl (requestHelpers.ts) reuses only the query from Neutron's absolute `next` href against the fixed base path, so there is no host/path injection; the concern is only resource exhaustion.
candidates.precedent: Both ports and routers list share the identical loop.
